Quick Start Guide

Mulai dalam 3 langkah sederhana supaya kamu langsung paham alurnya.

Step 1

🎯 Choose Today’s Challenge

Pilih day yang ingin kamu kerjakan lalu jalankan challenge utama yang tersedia hari ini.

Listening Speaking Reading Writing
Step 2

🔥 Complete Daily Tasks

Kerjakan challenge singkat setiap hari. Sedikit tapi konsisten akan jauh lebih efektif.

Step 3

📈 Track Statistics & Habit

Lihat progres, streak, analitik skill, dan habit dashboard untuk menjaga ritme belajar.

Fitur Utama MindShift English

Semua skill penting digabung dalam satu alur belajar harian.

🎧

Listening Challenge

Latih telinga memahami pengucapan native melalui media audio-video.

🎤

Speaking Challenge

📖

Reading Challenge

✍️

Writing Challenge

Latih menulis yang jelas, natural, dan relevan dengan prompt harian.

🧠

Reflection Challenge

Evaluasi progres, mindset, dan strategi agar belajar tetap konsisten.

Tutorial Cara Menggunakan

Ikuti alur ini agar hasil belajar maksimal dari hari pertama.

1. Login lalu buka menu Challenge

Masuk akun, lalu pilih menu Challenge untuk memulai day belajar yang tersedia.

2. Selesaikan step secara berurutan

Kerjakan Listening, Reading, Writing, dan Reflection sampai status hari itu complete.

3. Gunakan AI feedback untuk perbaikan

Review hasil speaking dan writing, lalu ulangi bagian yang masih lemah.

4. Pantau statistik dan habit dashboard

Lihat streak, progress rate, dan pola belajar mingguan agar konsistensi terjaga.

5. Ulangi besok dengan target kecil

Fokus daily progress. Tujuan utama adalah ritme harian, bukan perfeksionisme.

💡 Tips Agar Cepat Lancar

  • Konsisten 10 menit sehari lebih baik daripada 2 jam sesekali.
  • Fokus progress, bukan perfect.
  • Ulangi challenge speaking berkali-kali untuk meningkatkan confidence.
  • Jangan takut salah, karena koreksi adalah bagian dari growth.
  • Gunakan reflection untuk evaluasi diri dan rencana besok.

FAQ Mini

Berapa lama tiap challenge?

Rata-rata 5 sampai 10 menit per sesi, tergantung kedalaman latihanmu.

Harus urut?

Tidak wajib, tapi sangat disarankan urut agar progres skill lebih stabil.

Kalau skip sehari?

Streak bisa reset, jadi lebih baik tetap belajar singkat daripada berhenti total.

Bisa dari HP?

Bisa. Semua halaman sudah dirancang responsif dan nyaman untuk mobile.

❔ FAQ

How does MindShift English work?

MindShift English adalah challenge 100 hari dengan 4 langkah harian: Listening, Reading, Writing, dan Reflection. Pada hari milestone (10, 20, ... 100), kamu akan mengerjakan quiz untuk membuka badge.

Can I skip days?

Kamu tetap bisa membuka dan review hari mana pun. Namun untuk menjaga streak, selesaikan hari secara berurutan.

How are badges earned?

Badge didapat setelah lulus milestone quiz dengan skor minimal 70% di hari 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, dan 100.

Is my data saved?

Ya, progres disimpan secara lokal di browser. Saat integrasi Firebase aktif, data akan disinkronkan ke cloud.

What if I have technical issues?

Coba clear cache browser lalu reload halaman. Jika belum berhasil, hubungi support di support@mindshift.com.

🧭 Belajar Lebih Efektif

  • Selesaikan challenge harian di jam belajar yang sama setiap hari.
  • Ulangi listening minimal 3 kali untuk meningkatkan pronunciation.
  • Gunakan milestone quiz sebagai checkpoint pemahaman 10-harian.
  • Tulis reflection singkat agar progres lebih konsisten.

🗄️ Database Schema Reference

For developers: Complete guide to MindShift English data structures and validation rules

User Profile Document

{
  uid: "firebase-auth-id",
  email: "user@example.com",
  name: "John Doe",
  whatsapp: "+62812345678",
  origin: "Jakarta",
  joinedAt: "2026-03-08T10:30:00Z",
  createdAt: Timestamp(...),
  updatedAt: Timestamp(...),
}

User Progress Document

{
  userId: "firebase-auth-id",
  currentDay: 15,
  completedDays: [1,2,3,...,14],
  totalDaysCompleted: 14,
  streak: 5,
  lastCompletedDate: "2026-03-08T10:30:00Z",
  listeningScore: 85,
  readingScore: 78,
  writingScore: 92,
  averageScore: 85,
  tasksCompleted: {
    listening: ["day1", "day2", ...],
    reading: ["day1", "day2", ...],
    writing: ["day1", "day2", ...],
    reflection: ["day1", "day2", ...]
  },
  createdAt: Timestamp(...),
  updatedAt: Timestamp(...),
}

🔍 Profile Field Validation

Field Type Required Rules
uid string ✓ Yes 21-28 chars (Firebase UID)
email string ✓ Yes abc@example.com format
name string ✓ Yes Non-empty string
whatsapp string ✓ Yes Must match +62xxxxxxxxxx
origin string No Any string (optional)
joinedAt string ✓ Yes ISO 8601 timestamp

📊 Progress Field Validation

Field Type Min Max Notes
currentDay number 1 100 Integer only
streak number 0 ∞ Cannot be negative
totalDaysCompleted number 0 100 Cannot exceed 100
listeningScore number 0 100 Percentage (0-100)
readingScore number 0 100 Percentage (0-100)
writingScore number 0 100 Percentage (0-100)
averageScore number 0 100 Average of above

📍 Firestore Paths

/users/{userId}/data/profile - User profile document

/users/{userId}/data/progress - User progress document

/users/{userId}/activities/{activityId} - Activity log documents

⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid

❌ Don't: Skip validation before saving
✅ Do: Always validate data before persisting to database

❌ Don't: Use client timestamps
✅ Do: Use server timestamps via Firestore

❌ Don't: Forget user initialization
✅ Do: Initialize documents when user registers

❌ Don't: Trust unvalidated input
✅ Do: Validate all fields against schema rules

🔑 Key Takeaways

  • Always initialize user documents when registering
  • Always validate before saving any data
  • Email must be valid format (abc@example.com)
  • WhatsApp must start with +62
  • Scores must be 0-100 range
  • currentDay must be 1-100
  • Use server timestamps, not client time
  • Check health regularly with health checks

🔥 Firestore Database Schema

Complete structure and organization of MindShift English data in Firebase Firestore

📁 Collection Structure

firestore root
├── users/
│   └── {userId}/
│       ├── data/
│       │   ├── profile (document)
│       │   └── progress (document)
│       └── activities/
│           └── {activityId} (document)

👤 User Profile Model

Path: /users/{userId}/data/profile

{
  uid: "firebase-auth-id",
  email: "learner@example.com",
  name: "John Doe",
  whatsapp: "+628123456789",
  origin: "Jakarta",
  joinedAt: "2026-03-08T10:30:00Z",
  createdAt: Timestamp(...),
  updatedAt: Timestamp(...)
}

📊 User Progress Model

Path: /users/{userId}/data/progress

Key Fields:

  • currentDay: Number (1-100) - Current learning day
  • completedDays: Array - List of completed day numbers
  • streak: Number - Consecutive days completed
  • tasksState: Object - Completion status for each task type per day
  • listeningCounts: Object - Repetition counts for listening practice
  • readingFeedback: Object - Fluency, clarity, rhythm scores and feedback per day
  • writingInputs: Object - User rewrites and translations
  • dailyReflections: Array - Mood, habit ratings, and reflection notes
  • quizHistory: Array - Quiz scores and responses
  • createdAt/updatedAt: Timestamps - Account and update times

📝 Activity Logs Model

Path: /users/{userId}/activities/{activityId}

{
  userId: "firebase-auth-id",
  type: "registration|lesson_start|lesson_complete|quiz_submit",
  day: 5,
  data: { /* activity-specific data */ },
  timestamp: "2026-03-08T15:30:00Z",
  createdAt: Timestamp(...)
}

Activity Types:

  • registration - User account created
  • lesson_start - Started daily challenge
  • lesson_complete - Completed daily challenge with reflection
  • quiz_submit - Submitted milestone quiz

⚡ Indexing & Performance

Recommended Indexes:

1. Progress by Day
Collection: users/{userId}/data/progress
Field: currentDay (Ascending)

2. Activities by Timestamp
Collection: users/{userId}/activities
Field: timestamp (Descending)

3. Reflections Array Query
Collection: users/{userId}/data/progress
Field: dailyReflections (Array-contains)

🛡️ Firestore Best Practices

✅ Document Size: Max 1 MB per document (progress doc ~50-100 KB)

✅ Subcollections: Cleaner organization (data, activities) and better privacy isolation

✅ Timestamps: Use serverTimestamp() for system fields, ISO strings for user data

✅ Cost Optimization: Minimize reads, batch updates, archive old activities

✅ Security: All data private to user (see firestore.rules), logs for auditing

✅ Scalability: Ready for 10,000+ users with proper indexing

📈 Data Growth Estimates

Per User:

  • Profile doc: ~2 KB
  • Progress doc (at Day 100): ~50-100 KB
  • Activities (100 logs): ~20 KB
  • Total per user: ~75-125 KB

At Scale:

  • 1,000 users: ~100 MB
  • 10,000 users: ~1 GB
  • 100,000 users: ~10 GB

🔄 Data Migration Guide

From localStorage to Firestore:
1. Export localStorage data
2. Transform to Firestore format
3. Use Firebase Admin SDK for batch import
4. Verify data integrity post-migration
5. Update app to use real Firestore
6. Archive or delete old localStorage data

💡 Developer Tips

  • Always use subcollection paths to isolate user data
  • Use array-contains queries for reflecting on multiple elements
  • Index array fields if filtering frequently
  • Monitor Firestore usage in Firebase Console
  • Use transactions for multi-document updates
  • Consider batching for imports and migrations
  • Archive activity logs after 1 year to reduce costs
  • Use security rules to enforce data access patterns
